title: Gatekeeper
intro: File types that never belong in a release, kept out by your download clients and *arr apps. Every blocked download counts against the indexer that sent it.

hero.label: Blocked downloads
hero.caught_one: 1 download with a blocked file in the last {{days}} days.
hero.caught_other: {{count}} downloads with blocked files in the last {{days}} days.
hero.none: Nothing blocked in the last {{days}} days.
hero.unprotected: Not active in any service yet

setup.title: Decide which files never get through
setup.body: Pick the file types below, choose where they are blocked and switch the gatekeeper on. Wardarr writes the list into each service and keeps it there.
setup.step1: Pick file types: start with the presets.
setup.step2: Choose where: your download client is the best place, because it stops a file before it lands on disk.
setup.step3: Switch it on. From then on blocked downloads show up here and lower the score of the indexer that sent them.

map.title: Analysis map
map.help: Where blocked downloads came from and what they contained. Point at an indexer or a file type to follow it.
map.label: {{total}} blocked downloads: {{summary}}
map.hint: Point at an indexer or a file type to see its share.
map.indexerDetailNoGrabs: {{name}}: {{count}} blocked. No grabs from this indexer in the history.
map.emptyBody: When a download client or *arr app keeps out a file from your list, it shows up here with the indexer that sent it.
map.unknownHelp: SABnzbd only says that it found an unwanted file, not which one. Those downloads appear as "Type unknown".

impact.title: Effect on the indexers
impact.help: The indexer score with and without blocked downloads counted. Indexers that send none gain a little; indexers that send many lose up to 15 points.
impact.notCounted: Blocked downloads count towards the score once the gatekeeper is on.
impact.empty: No indexer has grabs in this time frame yet.

list.title: File types to block
list.help: A file with one of these extensions inside a download stops it. Entries you added by hand in a service stay there.
list.empty: No file types yet. Start with a preset.
list.invalid: That is not a file extension. Use letters and digits, like exe or ps1.

executables.name: Programs
executables.help: Files that run on their own, like exe, scr and msi.

scripts.name: Scripts and shortcuts
scripts.help: Files that run commands when opened, like bat, ps1, vbs and lnk.

archives.name: Unusual archives
archives.help: Archive formats no normal release uses, often used to hide something.

images.name: Disc images
images.help: iso, img and similar. Some real releases come as disc images, so only add these if you never want them.

targets.title: Where it is blocked
targets.help: Download clients stop a file before it is downloaded; *arr apps only notice it when they import. Blocking in the download client is recommended.
targets.none: None of your services can block file extensions. SABnzbd, qBittorrent, Sonarr and Radarr can.
targets.notSupported: Lidarr, NZBGet, Transmission and Deluge cannot block file extensions. Block them in your download client instead.

detail.downloader: Stops the download as soon as the file shows up.
detail.arr: Marks the download as failed at import, then searches for another release.
detail.partial_one: Cannot block {{list}}. This app only knows fixed groups of file types.
detail.partial_other: Cannot block {{list}}. This app only knows fixed groups of file types.
detail.drift: Missing {{list}}. Save to write them again.
detail.whitelist: SABnzbd only allows listed file types (whitelist mode). Wardarr does not change that.
detail.tooOld: This version cannot block file extensions. Update it to use the gatekeeper here.
detail.noIndexers: This app has no indexers to switch the check on for.
detail.error: Wardarr could not read the settings of this service.

options.sabAction: What SABnzbd does with such a download
options.sabActionHelp: Abort removes it right away so the *arr app can pick another release.
options.autoRepairHelp: Checks every 15 minutes and writes the list again when a service lost it, for example after a Prowlarr sync.

saved: Saved and written into the services.

recent.title: Recently blocked
recent.empty: Nothing blocked in this time frame.

redownload.title: Search again after a block
redownload.help: A blocked download is only replaced when the *arr app puts it on its blocklist and searches again (Settings → Download Clients → Failed Download Handling → Redownload Failed).
redownload.off: Redownload Failed is off: {{name}} keeps the failed download and does not search for another release.
redownload.noCompleted: Completed Download Handling is off, so {{name}} never notices a blocked download. Switch it on in {{name}}.
redownload.on: {{names}} blocklist a failed download and search again.
